summary: US President Trump called off a planned massive attack on Iran — described as the largest since WWII — after requests from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, and Iran, with new nuclear talks set to begin Monday. Israel eliminated two Hamas commanders, including a Nukhba commander who participated in the October 7 attack, and declared it will not withdraw from its current positions in Gaza. Oil prices dropped over 5% following the de-escalation signals.
key_points: Trump aborted a massive planned strike on Iran after regional allies and Iran requested talks; new negotiations start Monday with agreements on Hormuz Strait and denuclearization expected. (Source: @VahidOnline/77711)
Israel eliminated two Hamas operatives: Nukhba commander Abdullah Abu Alteif who infiltrated on Oct 7, and Daraj Tuffah Battalion commander Jalal Tzavich. (Source: @almogboker78/17889)
Israeli political source confirms Israel will not withdraw from current Gaza line and will continue thwarting threats. (Source: @almogboker78/17883)
Global oil prices fell over 5% after Trump announced halt to military action and new Iran talks, easing fears of Hormuz Strait closure. (Source: @VahidOnline/77713)
CENTCOM intelligence analysts tasked with finding "creative and unconventional ways to pressure and punish Iran" per senior officer email. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6033)
Suspected kidnapping in Samaria: Israeli vehicle stolen near Nabi Elias with 8-year-old girl; girl recovered in village after suspect fled; manhunt ongoing. (Source: @inon_yttach/9799)
Palestinian shot in serious condition by live fire on Jerusalem Street east of Nablus, northern West Bank. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/382725)
Iran executed two political prisoners, Amid Behzad and Pouria Safvat, for alleged espionage and intelligence cooperation with Israel. (Source: @mamlekate/104064)

sections.executive_summary: US President Trump called off a planned massive attack on Iran — described as the largest since WWII — after requests from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, and Iran, with new nuclear talks set to begin Monday. Israel eliminated two Hamas commanders, including a Nukhba commander who participated in the October 7 attack, and declared it will not withdraw from its current positions in Gaza. Oil prices dropped over 5% following the de-escalation signals.

points: Trump revealed he aborted a massive planned attack on Iran — potentially the largest since WWII — after Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, and Iran requested a halt; new talks begin Monday with agreements on Hormuz Strait access and Iranian denuclearization expected. (Source: @VahidOnline/77711)

Global oil prices dropped more than 5% on Monday after Trump announced the halt to military action and start of new talks, with markets citing reduced probability of military confrontation and Hormuz Strait closure. (Source: @VahidOnline/77713)

Iran executed two political prisoners, Amid Behzad and Pouria Safvat, on Monday (12 Mordad) for alleged espionage and intelligence cooperation with Israel, per judiciary-affiliated Mizan news agency. (Source: @mamlekate/104064)

CENTCOM intelligence analysts received an unusual email from a senior officer requesting "new creative and unconventional ways to pressure and punish Iran" to generate options for President Trump. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6033)

Trump stated Hormuz Strait is under full US Navy control and nothing passes to Iran unless a deal or surrender is reached; he insisted Iran will never obtain a nuclear weapon. (Source: @amitsegal/63606)

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a phone call discussing regional developments and diplomatic moves; Dar invited Araghchi to Islamabad. (Source: @VahidOnline/77721)

IDF and Shin Bet eliminated two Hamas operatives: Abdullah Adnan Taha Abu Alteif, a Nukhba commander who infiltrated Israel on October 7 and fought IDF throughout the war, and Jalal Tzavich, a Daraj Tuffah Battalion commander recently promoting terror plans. (Source: @almogboker78/17889)
An Israeli political source stated Israel will not withdraw from its current line in the Gaza Strip and will continue to thwart all threats to civilians and soldiers. (Source: @almogboker78/17883)

Defense Minister Katz ordered Gilboa Crossing to operate 24/7 for vehicular movement of Israeli residents of Northern Samaria for four months, to support infrastructure work for new settlements per government decision. (Source: @New_security8200/203162)

IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir reportedly opposes Defense Minister Katz's announcement of a replacement for Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, stating the appointment was not coordinated and he has no intention of replacing key commanders. (Source: @manniefabian/58917)

IDF documented an Islamic Jihad terrorist in uniform participating in the sixth phase of the "Sky Doors" hostage handover ceremony; the terrorist, who recently tried to advance terror plans against IDF and Israeli civilians, was eliminated. (Source: @idf_telegram/24820)

Suspected kidnapping attempt near Nabi Elias in Samaria: Israeli vehicle stolen with 8-year-old girl in back seat; vehicle drove into village near Azzun; IDF launched search; girl found in Nabi Elias after suspect threw her from vehicle and fled toward Azzun; girl reunited with her Arab-Israeli mother; manhunt underway. (Source: @inon_yttach/9799)
Palestinian young man shot with live fire in serious condition on Jerusalem Street east of Nablus, northern West Bank; ambulance crews evacuated him. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/382725)

Military prosecution filed indictment against Nur Shams Battalion commander Kamal Khatib for July 1, 2024 IED attack that killed Sgt. (res.) Yehuda Gato and injured another; Khatib remotely detonated IED from room in Balaa neighborhood via cellphone; indictment includes heading terror battalion, recruiting operatives, planting IEDs, arms dealing, transferring funds and equipment. (Source: @inon_yttach/9795)
Residents in the confrontation line reported interceptions seen and fired from fighter jets. (Source: @pkpoi/143501)
Artillery shelling reported on Meiss el-Jabal in southern Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/34571)
Husseini processions of Hashd al-Shaabi in Karbala displayed banners condemning Al Saud crimes against the Iraqi people. (Source: @naya_foriraq/86827)

Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar joined Iran in requesting Trump abort the planned massive attack on Iran, according to Trump's own account; they preferred a deal over military action fearing catastrophic regional consequences. (Source: @VahidOnline/77711)
Trump stated Hormuz Strait must be fully open tomorrow and is under US Navy control; nothing passes to Iran unless a deal or surrender is reached. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/382717)

Oil markets reacted to reduced military confrontation risk in the Middle East and increased hope for Tehran-Washington agreement, with concerns about oil supply disruption and Hormuz Strait closure easing. (Source: @VahidOnline/77713)

sections.threat_assessment: The immediate threat of a massive US-Iran military confrontation has been paused but not resolved, as Trump emphasizes the attack remains ready to execute if talks fail. Israel continues kinetic operations against Hamas leadership in Gaza while maintaining its positional stance, and West Bank violence persists with kidnapping attempts and shootings. The CENTCOM brainstorming for unconventional pressure on Iran suggests the US is preparing asymmetric options if diplomacy collapses. Iran's execution of alleged Israeli spies signals internal hardening. The situation remains highly volatile with multiple flashpoints capable of rapid escalation.
sections.regional_response: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar actively intervened to prevent US strikes on Iran, aligning with Iranian requests for diplomacy — a notable convergence of Gulf state and Iranian interests. Pakistan engaged Iran diplomatically with a foreign minister call and invitation to Islamabad. Oil markets responded positively to de-escalation signals. However, Trump's "last chance" rhetoric and the CENTCOM pressure campaign indicate the diplomatic window is narrow and backed by credible military threats.
sections.intelligence_notes: The IDF's public documentation of an Islamic Jihad operative in a hostage handover ceremony — followed by his elimination — demonstrates integrated intelligence-operational cycles targeting individuals across ceasefire mechanisms. The Nur Shams Battalion indictment reveals sustained Israeli legal-military pressure on West Bank militant infrastructure. The Gilboa Crossing 24/7 opening for Northern Samaria settlers indicates long-term Israeli settlement expansion planning. The Trump administration's use of regional allies as intermediaries to halt strikes suggests a coordinated diplomatic-military strategy.
